venue: ICSE 2024 Research Track (published as "Out of Sight, Out of Mind: Better Automatic Vulnerability Repair by Broadening Input Ranges and Sources")
structure_gain: Removing serialized AST sequence drops EM by 1.0pp (20.0%->19.0%); removing CWE knowledge drops it 1.1pp; removing full-function input drops it 1.2pp, all on the same adapted-CodeT5 backbone and training budget
confound_note: Ablation removes one input component at a time (full function / AST / CWE knowledge) while holding backbone (adapted-CodeT5) and training budget fixed, isolating each representation's contribution
stop_detail: No automated grounding/stop mechanism; qualitative case study only (Sec 6.1), relies on assumed perfect fault localization via special tokens marking vulnerable lines
threats_to_datum: Assumes perfect fault localization (not realistic deployment); EM metric can penalize semantically-correct but syntactically different patches (Sec 6.5 Threats to Validity)

key_numbers.metric: Pair accuracy gain vs code-level RAG baseline
key_numbers.where: Main results / comparison to code-level RAG

key_numbers.metric: Manual detection accuracy with generated explanations

structure_gain: Knowledge-level RAG (structured multi-dimensional vulnerability knowledge) beats code-level RAG (raw code retrieval) by 16-27 points pair accuracy; beats a fine-tuning baseline (LLMAO) by 22-26 points
confound_note: Compares knowledge-level RAG vs code-level RAG vs fine-tuned baseline -- retrieval content type differs across arms and the fine-tuning comparator changes the adaptation mechanism entirely, so representation is not cleanly isolated from model/training differences
stop_detail: Iteratively checks each retrieved knowledge item's vulnerability cause against the presence/absence of its fix before flagging code as vulnerable (knowledge-level RAG detection procedure)
threats_to_datum: Single language (C/C++, Linux kernel only); authors note generalizability to other LLMs requires further investigation (Limitations)

structure_gain: Removing the graph-to-text cross-modal alignment module (which fuses the CPG-derived GAT embeddings into soft prompts) drops accuracy by 14.5-18.75pp across three frozen LLM backbones, same soft-prompt tuning budget otherwise
confound_note: Ablation removes individual graph-fusion components (cross-modal alignment, projector, positional/type embeddings) one at a time while the frozen LLM backbone and PEFT training budget stay fixed -- a clean representation-fusion ablation
stop_detail: No natural-language grounding output: graph structure enters the LLM only as opaque continuous soft-prompt embeddings, not a readable/verifiable text trace (soft prompt tuning section)
threats_to_datum: Only 7B-parameter LLMs tested (hardware constraints); possible pretraining data contamination acknowledged but only partially mitigated by using latest DiverseVul release (Sec VII Threats to Validity)

structure_gain: Removing RAG (retrieved audit reports / similar-contract corpus) drops F1 from 0.9104 to 0.8440 (-6.64pp); a full-context variant LLM-BSCVM(E) that injects more retrieved text actually underperforms (80.42% accuracy) due to noise
confound_note: w/o-RAG ablation also implicitly changes the model-vs-retrieval evidence weighting (full model uses a 70/20 model/retrieval split); a separate w/o-Static-analysis arm removes a different component, so retrieval is not isolated from the static-analysis and weighting mechanisms
stop_detail: Patch Verification Agent runs a multi-agent debate among independent models to confirm a repair eliminates the vulnerability without introducing new ones before finalizing (Verifier agent description)
threats_to_datum: Repair success rate only ~21% under independent validation; auto-generated audit reports explicitly acknowledged as not yet matching human-expert reliability (Limitations)

key_numbers.value: 89% full; 64% w/o AST fragmentation; 60% w/o cross-file RAG; 77% w/o PoV guidance

structure_gain: w/o cross-file RAG (single-function context only) drops F1 from 89% to 60% (-29pp); w/o AST-based fragmentation drops F1 to 64% (-25pp); w/o PoV-guided reasoning drops F1 to 77% (-12pp), all on the same 57-project dataset
confound_note: Each ablation arm removes one mechanism (AST fragmentation, multi-agent cross-file RAG, or PoV guidance) on the same dataset, isolating that component's contribution reasonably cleanly, though underlying LLM/agent budget per arm is not explicitly confirmed identical
stop_detail: Reflector agent's retrieval loop terminates when it judges the assembled context provides sufficient inter-procedural coverage for exploitability determination or no new relevant fragments are retrieved (multi-agent RAG loop, Reflector/Grader description)
threats_to_datum: Ground truth relies on only two human annotators; PoV-guided reasoning applicable to only ~51% of vulnerabilities that have available PoV tests (Sec 6 Threats to Validity)

key_numbers.metric: F1 gain, optimized vs minimal-context prompt (OpenVuln)

structure_gain: Optimized prompt (flow-sensitive taint traces + CWE-specific micro-rubric) improves F1 by ~0.15 on average over a minimal-context baseline prompt with the same LLM and decoding settings, e.g. gpt-5 +0.334 F1 on OpenVuln (Table 4)
confound_note: Baseline-prompt vs optimized-prompt comparison holds the LLM and decoding (temperature=0, schema-constrained JSON) fixed and varies only the structured context content (taint trace + CWE rubric vs minimal alert text)
stop_detail: One-shot, schema-constrained JSON adjudication per alert with no iterative agent loop or fine-tuning; every prompt/response pair is logged for audit (LLM adjudication section)
threats_to_datum: gemini-2.5-pro F1 drops from 0.91 on synthetic OWASP to 0.37 on real-world OpenVuln, suggesting possible benchmark-specific overfitting (Threats to Validity)

key_numbers.metric: C/C++ F1, full vs no-reasoning ablation

key_numbers.value: 15 zero-day vulnerabilities found in actively maintained repos via project-level agent

structure_gain: Removing reasoning trajectories (VulnLLM-R-NoReason) drops C/C++ F1 from ~0.65 to ~0.58, with the largest degradation on out-of-distribution CWEs, on the same base model and otherwise matched training recipe
confound_note: Ablation arms (NoReason, single-teacher variants, NoSummary) each change one training-recipe component, but underlying training-data volume/composition can still shift slightly between arms since filtering yields differ
stop_detail: Reasoning generation is truncated at a fixed token budget (~8,192 tokens at eval, 32K max) forcing a final answer; the project-level agent scaffold caps tool-use interaction rounds for efficiency (inference / agent scaffold section)
threats_to_datum: Authors note frequent false positives 'because of lack of context'; possible data leakage flagged for commercial models with likely prior knowledge of well-known codebases like Nginx (Threats to Validity)

key_numbers.metric: PrimeVul accuracy, function-only vs full CPRVul

structure_gain: Appending raw/unstructured interprocedural context DEGRADES UniXcoder accuracy on PrimeVul (56.65%->54.22%), while CPG-derived, profiled+ranked context plus structured reasoning improves it to 67.78% (+11.13pp), holding the 1,024-token context window and fine-tuning budget (5 epochs) fixed across arms
confound_note: All arms share the same context-window size and fine-tuning schedule; only the representation of the added context (none / raw / GPT-4.1-profiled+ranked) and presence of explicit reasoning supervision vary
stop_detail: Model selection uses best checkpoint by validation-set performance; structured reasoning grounds the final label in explicit 'observation / security_reasoning / impact' JSON fields generated before the verdict (Phase II reasoning description)
threats_to_datum: Context profiling/ranking relies on GPT-4.1, so results may not transfer to open-source LLMs; evaluation uses class-balanced datasets only, unclear generalization to realistic class-imbalanced settings (Limitations)

key_numbers.metric: FPR escalation with text fine-tuning (Qwen3-8B, OWASP Java)
key_numbers.value: 0.763 zero-shot -> 0.866 pilot -> 1.000 full-scale, while F1 stays 0.637-0.688

key_numbers.metric: FPR reduction switching text-trained model's input to AST, no retraining (Qwen3-8B)

key_numbers.value: FPR reduction of Delta=-0.527 under text->AST switch

structure_gain: Switching a text-fine-tuned model's inference-time input from raw text to pruned AST (no retraining) cuts FPR by 0.282-0.527 depending on CWE, with only a modest F1 cost (e.g. 0.688->0.637 for Qwen3-8B), same model weights and training budget -- a pure representation-only manipulation
confound_note: Full factorial design fixes the base model and LoRA training budget while independently varying training-time representation (text/AST) and inference-time representation (text/AST), including a cross-representation probe that isolates representation from training adaptation
stop_detail: No grounding/stop mechanism reported; this is an empirical characterization study without a deployable technique or explicit stopping criterion
threats_to_datum: Restricted to intra-procedural code units by design; only two 8B models and two target languages tested; ~9.9% of BenchmarkPython samples excluded for being AST-unparseable, a potential selection bias (Limitations)

demote_reason: Full text confirms all five prompt designs (low-effort, simple general/specific, advanced general/specific CoT) feed the LLM identical raw full-source-code text for each WordPress plugin; only natural-language instruction wording/CoT structure and whether the CWE class is disclosed vary. No AST/CFG/taint/call-graph representation or retrieval/context mechanism is used or studied -- purely a prompt-wording and model comparison over unstructured raw text (Methodology / prompt design section).

key_numbers.value: 75.0% on 200-CVE strict subset; abstract reports 73% overall, outperforming strongest baseline by 29pp
w/o code-structure -1.5pp, w/o execution context -0.5pp, w/o commit-history -2.0pp (75.0% -> 73.0-74.5%)

structure_gain: Removing any single context facet (code-structure/data-flow, runtime-execution, or commit-history) costs only 0.5-2pp success rate (75.0%->73.0-74.5%) on the same model (GPT-5.2) and multi-agent scaffold, showing the three facets are complementary rather than individually dominant; collapsing to a single-agent scaffold costs 44.5pp
confound_note: Context-facet ablations hold the model (GPT-5.2) and multi-agent scaffold fixed while removing one context type at a time, cleanly isolating each facet; separate ablations of model capacity (GPT-5-mini) and agent scaffold (single vs multi-agent) are not representation-only and confound architecture with context
stop_detail: Repair subagent's synthesis-verification loop stops when the AddressSanitizer/sanitizer reproduction harness reports no violation, or after a 75-step budget is exhausted (synthesis-verification loop description)
threats_to_datum: Evaluated only on SEC-Bench C/C++ memory-safety vulnerabilities; authors explicitly flag the need for further study on other languages and vulnerability types (Limitations); patch novelty checked via Jaccard similarity (avg 0.1177) to rule out memorization
